title: Typhoon Champi Could Reach Taiwan Next Week
summaryZh: 颱風昌鴻下週四可能接近台灣東方海面，不排除登陸。
summaryHi: टाइफ़ून चैंपी अगले गुरुवार ताइवान के पूर्वी समुद्र तक पहुँच सकता है।
summaryEs: El tifón Champi podría acercarse al este de Taiwán el próximo jueves.
summaryJa: 台風チャンピーが来週木曜に台湾東方沖へ接近し、上陸の可能性も。
summaryKo: 태풍 참피가 다음 주 목요일 대만 동쪽 해상에 접근할 수 있다.
summaryEn: Typhoon Champi may reach waters east of Taiwan next Thursday and could even cross the island.
paragraphs: Typhoon Champi may approach Taiwan, or possibly sweep across it, later next week, according to the latest forecast from the Central Weather Administration (CWA).

As of 2pm on Saturday, the storm's centre lay roughly 2,980 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, the island's southernmost tip. It was heading west at 22 kilometres per hour, packing maximum sustained winds of 162 kilometres per hour and a radius of 180 kilometres.

Forecaster Chang Cheng-chuan said Champi was likely to intensify as it moved west before veering west-northwest towards the waters east of Taiwan. Once it arrives there on Thursday, it is expected to curve gradually northward.

The track, however, remains uncertain. Chang explained that if the Pacific high-pressure system holds firm, it could steer the typhoon on a more westerly course, and several models already show it crossing the island.
Residents can expect fair to cloudy skies until Tuesday, with rain arriving from Wednesday, particularly in the north and northeast.
A strong storm called Typhoon Champi is far away in the Pacific Ocean. It may come near Taiwan next week.
On Saturday afternoon, the storm was almost 3,000 kilometres from the south of Taiwan. It was moving west. Its winds were very fast, about 162 kilometres an hour.
Taiwan's weather office says the storm may get stronger. It may arrive in the sea east of Taiwan next Thursday. Then it may turn north.
But some computer models show a different path. The storm may go further west and cross Taiwan.
The weather will be good until Tuesday. From Wednesday, there will be rain, mostly in the north.
Typhoon Champi, a powerful storm in the western Pacific, could come close to Taiwan or even cross the island next week, Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA) said on Saturday.

At 2pm on Saturday, the typhoon was about 2,980 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, the southernmost point of Taiwan. It was moving west at 22 kilometres per hour, with maximum winds of 162 kilometres per hour.
CWA forecaster Chang Cheng-chuan said Champi could become stronger as it travels west. It is expected to reach the waters off eastern Taiwan next Thursday and then slowly turn north.
However, the path is not certain. If a high-pressure system over the Pacific stays strong, it could push the typhoon further west, and some forecast models show it crossing Taiwan.

Until next Tuesday, the weather should be fair to cloudy across most of the island. Rain is expected to start from Wednesday, especially in northern and northeastern areas, so people should check the latest weather news.
Typhoon Champi may approach Taiwan, or possibly sweep across it, later next week, according to the latest forecast from the Central Weather Administration (CWA).

As of 2pm on Saturday, the storm's centre lay roughly 2,980 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, the island's southernmost tip. It was heading west at 22 kilometres per hour, packing maximum sustained winds of 162 kilometres per hour and a radius of 180 kilometres.

Forecaster Chang Cheng-chuan said Champi was likely to intensify as it moved west before veering west-northwest towards the waters east of Taiwan. Once it arrives there on Thursday, it is expected to curve gradually northward.

The track, however, remains uncertain. Chang explained that if the Pacific high-pressure system holds firm, it could steer the typhoon on a more westerly course, and several models already show it crossing the island.
Residents can expect fair to cloudy skies until Tuesday, with rain arriving from Wednesday, particularly in the north and northeast.

Taiwan could face a direct encounter with Typhoon Champi next week, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) has warned, although forecasters stress that the storm's eventual path is far from settled.

On Saturday afternoon the typhoon was positioned some 2,980 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, Taiwan's southernmost point, tracking west at 22 kilometres per hour. Its maximum sustained winds had reached 162 kilometres per hour, and its circulation extended across a radius of 180 kilometres.

According to CWA forecaster Chang Cheng-chuan, Champi is expected to gather strength as it heads west, subsequently veering west-northwest towards the seas off eastern Taiwan, which it could reach on Thursday before gradually swinging north.

Much hinges on the Pacific high-pressure system. Should it remain robust, Chang said, it could force the typhoon onto a more westerly trajectory, a scenario in which some models have it crossing the island outright.
In the meantime, conditions are forecast to stay fair to cloudy through Tuesday, with rain setting in from Wednesday, most notably in northern and northeastern regions.

Taiwan may be confronted with a potentially hazardous typhoon next week, as Typhoon Champi advances across the western Pacific, although meteorologists emphasise that considerable uncertainty surrounds its ultimate trajectory.

According to the Central Weather Administration (CWA), the system was located approximately 2,980 kilometres east-southeast of Eluanbi, the island's southernmost extremity, at 2pm on Saturday. It was travelling west at 22 kilometres per hour, with maximum sustained winds of 162 kilometres per hour and a radius of 180 kilometres.

CWA forecaster Chang Cheng-chuan anticipates that Champi will intensify progressively as it moves west, before veering west-northwest towards the waters east of Taiwan. Having reached that area on Thursday, it would be expected to recurve gradually to the north.

Nevertheless, this outcome is contingent on the behaviour of the Pacific high-pressure system. Were that system to remain dominant, it could deflect the typhoon onto a more westerly path; indeed, several forecast models already project a direct crossing of the island.
For the time being, the public can anticipate fair to cloudy weather until Tuesday, after which rain is predicted from Wednesday, predominantly in the north and northeast.
